introduction.value: Claude Code cross-referenced an EOB and policy documents in about three minutes and showed the author owed nothing beyond what they already paid; it did not file anything.

source_text.body:
Explain a denied insurance claim from EOB and policy
Claude Code cross-referenced an EOB and policy documents in about three minutes and showed the author owed nothing beyond what they already paid; it did not file anything.
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
The author made a new Git repo for personal insurance, with a CLAUDE.md, a filing schema, a journal and a README. This took about 15 minutes. He dropped in the Aetna EOB and his policy documents and asked Claude Code to explain the denied claim. Claude then offered to draft an email to the dentist, but the source doesn't say it sent one.
How it went
In about three minutes Claude explained that the plan excludes comprehensive dental services. It also showed that the $1,316 "Your Share" was the billed amount, while the in-network rate was $723.83, which he was already paying.
Worth knowing
The EOB's "Your Share" column showed the full billed amount, not the contracted in-network rate. Check that difference before assuming you owe more.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
I'm putting my Explanation of Benefits at [path to EOB file] and my policy documents in [folder path] in the same folder. Read them and explain why this claim was denied or reduced, what I actually owe, and whether the amount matches my plan's deductible, copay and coinsurance. Give me a short plain-English summary plus the exact policy language you relied on, and do not contact anyone or file anything.
Original source: https://common-sense.com/insights/insurance-denial-resolved-before-coffee/
